judgments.reason: Rules state the winner pays the bid, gains the lot, then receives a three-coin commission; bids also cannot exceed your coins when committing. Nothing supports bidding above available coins — the commission is awarded after payment and cannot be used to validate an over-sized bid.

The transcript shows the clerk revealing committed rival bids while the focal player is already committed; it does not show that waiting reveals rival bids prior to your own commitment. The model articulation does not state that waiting reveals rival bids before you commit.

The specification explicitly defines [close: 1] as settling after all three lots are sold. The evidence and play trace never show an ability to close early; thus the claimed terminal condition is incorrect.

The rules state the three-coin commission is given to the auction winner after paying and gaining the lot; catalog purchases are explicitly described as not auction wins. There is no evidence that catalog buys receive the auction commission.
